newsitem.title: INDIA: India communists firmly opposed to oil price rises.
newsitem.headline: India communists firmly opposed to oil price rises.

text.p: India's main communist parties, who are key partners in the ruling United Front coalition, reiterated their opposition to any proposal to raise petroleum product prices at a crucial meeting later on Monday.

The United Front's policy-making Steering Committee is scheduled to meet at 5 p.m. (1130 GMT) to discuss the politically sensitive issue. "We are still opposing the increases. We have not changed our stance," Sitaram Yechury, a senior leader of Communist Party of India (Marxist) and a member of the Steering Committee, told Reuters.
Yechury denied a news agency report that said the CPI(M) was not opposed to a proposal for raising petroleum product prices.

"We want the government to see other options," said D. Raja, a senior leader of the Communist Party of India (CPI) and another member of the Steering Committee. "We oppose the oil price hike. It is an easy way out yielding to the pressures of the market forces."

The CPI (M) has submitted an alternative plan to the Steering Committee that seeks to avoid what it views as a crippling rise in oil prices and calls for the government to return to the state-run oil sector surplus funds taken from it by earlier governments as well as the elimination of customs and excise duties.
Any increase in prices this week would be the second by the United Front coalition in its one year in power.
